summary.headline: CSB Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 22% QoQ to Rs.183 Cr, with NIM up to 3.81% and ROA to 1.29%.
summary.overview: CSB Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs.183 Cr, up 22% QoQ and 14% YoY, with net interest income of Rs.510 Cr (up 7% QoQ, 20% YoY). NIM widened to 3.81% from 3.66% in Q1, driven by a higher yield on advances (10.92%) and stable cost of funds. Fee income rebounded 20% QoQ, though overall fee income was down about 22% YoY due to market-linked non-core lines. Asset quality improved on GNPA (1.58%) and NNPA (0.33%), with credit cost at 24 bps, though elevated write-offs of fully provided card and unsecured book were flagged. Management said it is entering a "scale phase" with retail liability build-out, SME growth restarting, and guidance of ROA 1.5% to 1.8% next year.

financial_highlights.change: +20% QoQ; ex-treasury +27% QoQ; fee income -22% YoY
vs 3.66% in Q1 FY27 and 3.81% in Q2 FY26
Yield on advances 10.92% vs 10.65% in Q1
PCR 87.65% (79.19% without PWO); credit cost 24 bps

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book grew 36% YoY, but tonnage fell about 6% YoY and disbursements slowed; management targets gold at about 50% of loan mix by year-end (53% last year, 54% last quarter), with a 32% glide path by 2030. Gold yields rose about 50 bps QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate / wholesale
segments.commentary: Corporate segment grew 44% YoY; wholesale split roughly equally across corporate banking, mid-market and FIs, with corporate and mid-market growing faster.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: SME growth remained flattish after exits and customer losses on pricing; management expects SME growth to resume from this quarter after portfolio issues were corrected.

segments.name: Retail (ex-gold)
segments.commentary: Retail growth was muted; the bank degrew loan against security (repledge gold loans, now almost zero) and is keeping unsecured cards, agri and MFI cautious, with unsecured retail to restart around FY2028.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Core fee grew about 27% YoY and is just short of 15% of total income; overall fee is just short of 17% of total income (vs 23% last year, which included one-offs). Non-core lines (PSLC, treasury) declined.

guidance_outlook: ROA this year expected between 1.30% and 1.5%; next year (FY28) targeted at 1.5% to 1.8%, closer to 1.5% initially.
NIM guided at around 3.75% to 3.8% this year; around 3.75% next year.
Cost of funds to be brought down from 6.55% to about 6% next financial year.
Fee to total income assumed at 17% to 18%; IRDAI corporate agency draft may cut this by 0.5% to 1%.
Balance sheet growth guided at 30% to 50% faster than the system; system growth was faster this quarter due to FCNR inflows.
CASA to grow faster than term deposits from FY2028, after being slower this year.
Gold loans to fall to about 50% of mix by year-end; SBS 2030 targets continue.
capex_capacity: Network of 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at September 2026.
Core system upgrade and DC-DR switch completed; OFSAA implementation under way.
Technology investments span transaction banking (supply chain, CMS, trade), OBDX, corporate net banking and corporate LOS.
Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition the current focus.
Opex up about 11% QoQ and about 3% YoY; other opex up 18% QoQ mainly on technology, plus distribution and infrastructure; staff cost up about 17% YoY.
demand_pricing: Gold disbursements fell as rebooking is no longer shown as new disbursement and gold prices dipped; management says the regulator's LTV cut from 90% to 75% was managed.
Gold loan LTV about 75% vs 60-65% at peers, attributed to a larger agri portfolio where higher LTV is allowed; about 28% of gold book is above Rs.20 lakh ticket size.
Gold yields raised by about 50 bps QoQ, leveraging distribution and competitor pricing.
Lost some SME customers on pricing; exited a list of customers after quality review.
Deposit mix about 48% retail and 52% wholesale; FCY, CDs and borrowings remain significant funding sources.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other opex rise 18% QoQ and is it linked to higher other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total opex rose about 11% QoQ and 3% YoY; the rise was mainly technology, plus distribution expansion and infrastructure spends. Staff cost was up about 17% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in yield on advances and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Better asset quality, careful yield management in wholesale and SME, and a gold yield increase of about 50 bps QoQ, helped by distribution reach and competitor pricing. Cost of funds was flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why were write-offs high while credit cost was low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wrote off a fully provided vintage of credit card and unsecured loans with low recovery prospects and no PSL benefit; it said this had no impact on credit cost, which was 24 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI corporate agency consultation paper on fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, so guidance may drop from 18% to 17% short term, with the bank aiming to recover through core fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet growth outlook and retail deposit traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated growth 30% to 50% faster than system; retail current account acquisition has started, and liability franchise takes two to three years to build. Asset growth is not the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is Fairfax or IDBI relevant to CSB, and is there a Fairfax deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fairfax has no deposits with the bank and the board has not discussed the Fairfax/IDBI matter; the transaction is still incomplete.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROA and NIM outlooks for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of 1.30-1.5% this year, 1.5-1.8% next year; NIM around 3.75-3.8%, with cost of funds targeted at about 6% next year to offset mix shift.

risks_watch: Gold loan tonnage down about 6% YoY and gold disbursements slowing; gold book mix must fall to about 50%.
Regulatory fee risk from IRDAI corporate agency draft; fee-to-income could fall 0.5-1%.
Asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm; management points to a declining non-gold SMA book.
Cost of funds at 6.55% and reliance on FCY borrowings, CDs and bulk deposits; CASA ratio slipped to 18.96%.
Opex growth (other opex +18% QoQ) and cost-to-income at 64.8% against the fee and NIM outlook.
Interpretation risk on write-offs: elevated write-offs of fully provided book alongside PCR rising to 87.65%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on earnings momentum, ROA and the scale phase, but guarded on the timing of retail growth, CASA recovery and the fee impact from the IRDAI draft. Management declined to elaborate on the other income breakup and deflected the Fairfax/IDBI question as not yet relevant.
key_quotes: Overall, we had a fairly good quarter.

We will start seeing the growth on the SME side from this quarter onwards because most of the portfolio-related issues we faced in SME book for the last one-and-a-half years have been by and large corrected now.
I would say that we would aim to bring down the cost of funds to somewhere around 6% next financial year, which will give us a 50-basis points lift.

adds.what: Branch and ATM network at 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at September 2026 (no new branch additions guided)

growth.why: FY27 ROA guidance cut to 1.30-1.50% (from a higher implied range) and CASA-over-TD growth pushed to FY28, while balance sheet is guided at 30-50% faster than system and NIM held at ~3.75-3.8%; growth backing rests on gold-loan mix, wholesale corporate growth and retail liability launches rather than specific new capacity.
